title: Hellenism
lead: The spread of Greek language, cities, schools and ways of life through the lands Alexander conquered, from the 300s BC on. For Jews it raised the question of how far one could live as a Greek and remain faithful to the law. In Jerusalem a party of priests and leading men embraced Greek ways and built a gymnasium (1 Maccabees 1:11–15; 2 Maccabees 4:7–17); the persecution under Antiochus IV and the Maccabean revolt grew out of that struggle. Even the books that resisted it, such as 2 Maccabees and Wisdom, were written in Greek.
